messages:
maya_cs: ACME reported 403s for /v1/embeddings right after they rotated their SSO service token. They say token.inspect shows embeddings in the scp claim but API returns insufficient_scope. Repro they sent:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'
# -> 403 {\"error\":\"insufficient_scope\",\"message\":\"missing inference.embeddings\"}
```

maya_cs: They pasted the decoded JWT payload (scp field):
```
{"scp":"inference.generate;inference.embeddings;inference.rerank"}
```

ben_eng: Can you paste the raw header+payload (signature omitted) or at minimum the raw scp string? Curious if delimiter is a literal semicolon vs space.

maya_cs: Pasted the raw header+payload into the internal ticket. Confirmed: the scp value is semicolon-delimited.

ben_eng: That'll do it. Our auth matcher expects space-separated scopes per RFC (token.scp.split(/\s+/)). Semicolons won't match so the embeddings permission check fails even though humans see the scope present. :grimacing:

zara_prod: How would a semicolon make it in? ACME uses Azure AD SCIM provisioning with an older app template from a vendor. Some older provisioning templates join scopes with ';' for legacy integrations.

maya_cs: Customer confirmed they used a vendor-managed SCIM template created in 2021. When they renewed the app the delimiter behavior stayed the same and the rotated token kept the semicolon scp.

sam_oncall: Reproduced in staging: created a token with scp=\"inference.generate;inference.embeddings\". /v1/generate works (we apparently allow generate via a different check), but /v1/embeddings returns 403. Confirmed code path does exact token.scp.split(' ').includes(required).

ben_eng: Quick mitigation in authlib: fallback to accept common delimiters when parsing scp. Patch idea:
```js
let raw = token.payload.scp || '';
let scopes = raw.trim().length ? raw.split(/\s+/) : [];
if (!scopes.includes(requiredScope)) {
  // tolerate legacy delimiters as fallback
  scopes = raw.split(/[;:,|]+\s*/);
}
if (!scopes.includes(requiredScope)) throw new InsufficientScope();
```
I'll open a small PR to normalize parsing and add unit tests.

zara_prod: Also schedule a one-off migration to normalize historical SCIM-provisioned tokens in the DB (replace semicolons with spaces) and write audit records. We'll need a rollback plan and owner for the migration.

maya_cs: For the customer: temporary workaround is to create a Console API key (not SSO) or have their IdP admin re-provision the SCIM app with the updated template. I sent those instructions and asked for a sample token if they want us to triage directly.

ben_eng: PR created: authlib/normalize-scp + tests. Plan: canary to staging tonight, full prod rollout tomorrow morning if QA green. @deploy-bot please schedule canary.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: authlib/normalize-scp -> 2026-03-18T00:45:00Z. Infra on-call notified.

sam_oncall: Verified in staging after patch: tokens with semicolons now succeed on /v1/embeddings. Added regression test for semicolon-delimited scp and an integration test for tokens from SCIM import pipeline.

maya_cs: I'll tell the customer to rotate their SSO-issued token after we release (their older token may be cached on their side). I'll follow up and close once they confirm. Thanks everyone :pray:

ben_eng: Action items:
- merge patch (done)
- schedule DB migration to normalize legacy scp values (assigned)
- add SSO troubleshooting note to docs + sample idp reprovision steps
- notify support playbook about this delimiter edge case

maya_cs: Closing when customer confirms rotation fixed it on their end.
